breakfast.name: Tô (Millet Porridge)
instructions: Boil water
Stir in millet flour
Cook 10 min until thick
Shape into balls
Serve with sauce

breakfast.name: Beignets de Banane
instructions: Mash bananas, mix with flour and sugar
Fry spoonfuls until golden

breakfast.name: Bouillie de Fonio (Fonio Porridge)
ingredients: Fonio grain (Guinea's ancient grain — one of Africa's oldest cultivated cereals)
instructions: Wash fonio thoroughly — it's tiny and needs multiple rinses
Toast fonio briefly in a dry pot for nutty flavor
Add milk or water, stir continuously
Cook 15-20 min until thick and creamy like porridge
Add sugar, peanut butter, cinnamon
Fonio is gluten-free, nutrient-dense, and grows in poor soil where other grains fail
Guinea is fonio's heartland — this ancient grain has fed West Africa for 5000+ years
The grain is having a global moment as a 'superfood' — but Guinea knew first
breakfast.description: Guinea's ancient grain porridge — fonio, one of Africa's oldest cultivated cereals (5000+ years), cooked into thick, creamy porridge with peanut butter and cinnamon. Fonio is now viral globally as a gluten-free superfood, but Guinea has been eating it since before the pyramids were built.

breakfast.name: Fried Sweet Potato with Sauce
ingredients: Onion-pepper sauce: onion, hot pepper, oil, salt
instructions: Peel and slice sweet potatoes into thick rounds
Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy outside, soft inside
Make quick sauce: sauté sliced onion with hot pepper, add Maggi
Serve fried sweet potato with the onion-pepper sauce
Simple, cheap, filling — this is Guinea's everyday street breakfast
The sweetness of the potato against the spicy-savory sauce is the draw
breakfast.description: Guinean breakfast street food — thick slices of sweet potato fried golden and served with a spicy onion sauce. Simple, cheap, satisfying. The sweet-spicy contrast represents West African street food at its most fundamental.

lunch.name: Riz Gras (One-Pot Rice)
instructions: Brown meat, set aside
Sauté onions, tomatoes, paste
Add rice, vegetables, water
Cook covered until rice is done
Top with meat
lunch.description: West African one-pot rice with meat and vegetables.

lunch.name: Sauce Arachide (Peanut Sauce)
instructions: Brown chicken
Sauté onion, garlic, tomatoes
Add peanut paste and water
Return chicken, simmer 30 min
Serve with rice

lunch.name: Mafé (Peanut Butter Stew)
instructions: Brown meat in oil
Sauté onion, garlic, add tomato paste — fry until paste darkens
Add peanut butter — stir it in thoroughly, it becomes the sauce base
Add water to create a thick, creamy stew consistency
Add vegetables: sweet potato, cabbage, eggplant
Simmer 40 min until meat is tender and vegetables are cooked
The sauce should be thick, rich, and deeply peanutty
Season with Maggi, salt, pepper
Serve over rice — the peanut sauce over white rice is iconic West African
Mafé is Guinea, Mali, and Senegal's shared treasure — each version slightly different
lunch.description: Guinea's peanut butter stew — meat and vegetables simmered in a thick, rich peanut sauce. Mafé is West Africa's most beloved stew, and Guinea's version (heavier on the peanut, served with root vegetables) is deeply satisfying. The 'peanut butter as a savory stew base' concept continues to go viral globally.

lunch.name: Plasas (Cassava Leaf Stew)
instructions: Pound cassava leaves — traditionally in a large mortar, for a long time until very fine
Boil pounded leaves for 30 min to reduce bitterness
In separate pot, cook meat until tender
Add palm oil — it turns the stew a rich orange-red
Add smoked fish (the smoky umami is essential)
Add the cooked cassava leaves to the meat pot
Simmer together 20-30 min until everything melds
The palm oil and smoked fish create an incredibly deep, complex flavor
Season with Maggi, pepper
Serve over rice — the thick green-orange stew on white rice is visually striking
lunch.description: Guinea's cassava leaf stew — pounded cassava leaves cooked with palm oil, smoked fish, and meat into a thick, deeply flavored stew. The hand-pounding of the leaves (an hour of work) and the palm-oil-smoked-fish flavor combination make plasas a celebration of West African technique and patience.

lunch.name: Riz Gras (Fat Rice — Guinean Jollof)
instructions: Fry onion and garlic in oil until golden
Add tomato paste — fry until it darkens and oil separates (the key step)
Add meat, brown in the tomato base
Add water, vegetables, bring to boil
Add rice, stir once, cover tightly
Cook on low heat until rice absorbs all liquid — 25-30 min
The tomato-stained rice should be fluffy and separate, not sticky
Each grain should be coated in the tomato-oil mixture
This is Guinea's answer to jollof rice — and yes, there's a rivalry
lunch.description: Guinea's riz gras — tomato-stained, oil-rich one-pot rice that enters the great West African 'who makes the best rice' debate alongside Nigerian jollof, Ghanaian jollof, and Senegalese thiéboudienne. Guinea's version uses more palm oil, creating a richer, more orange result.

dinner.name: Poulet Yassa (Lemon-Onion Chicken)
instructions: Marinate chicken in lemon, onion, garlic 1 hour
Brown chicken, set aside
Cook onions until soft and golden
Add mustard and marinade, return chicken
Simmer 20 min, add olives
dinner.description: Tangy lemon and caramelized onion chicken.

dinner.name: Fouti (Cassava Leaf Stew)
instructions: Pound and boil cassava leaves 30 min
Add palm oil, fish, onion
Simmer until thick
Serve with rice
dinner.description: Cassava leaf stew with smoked fish.

dinner.name: Poulet Yassa (Guinean Variation)
instructions: Marinate chicken in lemon juice, onions, garlic, mustard, pepper — overnight is best
Remove chicken from marinade, brown in oil
In the same oil, cook the massive amount of marinated onions — they must caramelize completely
This takes 20+ min — the onions go from raw to golden to deeply caramelized
Add mustard, return chicken to pot with the onion sauce
Simmer 20 min until chicken is cooked through
The onion-lemon-mustard sauce should be thick and tangy
The ratio of onion to chicken is extreme — and that's correct
Serve over rice — the onion sauce is the star, the chicken is the vehicle
dinner.description: Guinea's poulet yassa — chicken buried in an avalanche of caramelized onions, lemon juice, and mustard. The extreme onion-to-chicken ratio and the tangy-sweet caramelized onion sauce make yassa one of West Africa's most famous dishes. The 'that's too many onions' reaction (it's never too many) is viral.

dinner.name: Sauce Feuilles (Leaf Sauce) with Fufu
instructions: Cook leaves until very tender — 20 min
In separate pot, make the base: fry onion, add palm oil, smoked fish
Add fresh fish or meat, cook through
Add the cooked leaves, mix thoroughly
Simmer until thick and rich — 20-30 min
The palm oil gives the sauce its characteristic orange-green color
Make fufu: bring water to boil, add cassava flour, stir vigorously until smooth and stretchy
Fufu should be smooth, elastic, and form a clean ball
Pinch fufu with fingers, make an indent, scoop up the leaf sauce — swallow without chewing
dinner.description: Guinean sauce feuilles with fufu — potato leaves cooked in palm oil with smoked fish, served with stretchy cassava fufu. The fufu technique (pinch, scoop, swallow without chewing) is one of West Africa's most viral food moments for the uninitiated.

dinner.name: Thiéboudienne (Guinean Fish and Rice)
ingredients: Whole fish (thiof/grouper or any firm white fish)
Vegetables: cassava, eggplant, cabbage, carrot, okra
instructions: Stuff fish with parsley-garlic-pepper paste (rof) — push into scored slits
Fry fish briefly in palm oil, set aside
Fry tomato paste in the same oil until very dark — this is the base
Add water, vegetables, tamarind — cook until vegetables are tender
Remove vegetables, add rice to the pot — cook in the vegetable-tomato broth
The rice absorbs all the flavors — tomato, fish, tamarind
Arrange on a large platter: rice on bottom, fish on top, vegetables around the sides
Everyone eats from the same platter — communal eating
The host assigns sections of the platter — everyone gets fish, rice, and vegetables
dinner.description: Guinea's thiéboudienne — the famous West African fish and rice, with fish stuffed with herb paste, cooked in tomato-tamarind broth, and served communally on a giant platter. The communal platter and the 'host assigns your section' tradition make thiéboudienne one of the most social meals in the world.

snacks.name: Fataya (Meat Turnovers)
ingredients: Filling: ground beef, onion, parsley, egg
instructions: Make dough, roll circles
Fill with seasoned beef
Fold, seal edges
Deep fry until golden

snacks.name: Beignets (Fried Dough)
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, yeast, egg, vanilla, milk — make a soft dough
Let rise 30 min until doubled
Pull off small pieces, shape into balls or rings
Deep fry until puffed and golden — they should be light and airy
Drain briefly, roll in sugar if desired
These are Guinea's universal street snack — every corner, every market
The morning beignet with coffee is Guinean urban life
Cheap, warm, satisfying — fried dough transcends all cultures
snacks.description: Guinean beignets — light, puffy fried dough balls sold at every street corner and market. The French colonial influence meets West African street food culture. Morning beignets with café are Guinea's Conakry urban ritual.

snacks.name: Alloco (Fried Plantain with Spicy Sauce)
instructions: Slice ripe plantain diagonally — thick pieces
Deep fry until deep golden and caramelized
Make quick sauce: onion, tomato, Scotch bonnet, Maggi
Serve hot plantain with the spicy sauce
The sweet plantain against the savory-spicy sauce is perfect
This is West Africa's universal fried snack — Guinea's version includes the onion sauce
snacks.description: Guinea's alloco — fried ripe plantain with a fiery onion-tomato sauce. Sweet meets spicy in West Africa's most beloved fried snack. The caramelized plantain edges and the burn of the pepper sauce are universal West African comfort.

snacks.name: Kola Nuts (Cultural Snack)
instructions: Break kola nut into lobes
Chew slowly — the bitterness gives way to a slightly sweet aftertaste
Kola nuts contain caffeine — they are a natural stimulant
They are shared at every important social occasion — weddings, naming ceremonies, meetings
Offering kola is a sign of respect and welcome in Guinean culture
The bitter flavor is acquired but deeply cultural
Kola nuts are the origin of 'cola' in Coca-Cola — the original recipe used kola nut extract
Chew with water — the water tastes sweet after the bitter nut
snacks.description: Guinea's most culturally significant food — the kola nut, shared at every ceremony and meeting as a sign of respect. Bitter, caffeinated, and the original ingredient behind 'Coca-Cola.' The cultural protocol of sharing kola and the Coca-Cola origin story are perpetually fascinating.

desserts.name: Degué (Millet and Yogurt)
instructions: Steam millet couscous
Mix with yogurt, sugar, vanilla, cream
Chill and serve
desserts.description: Creamy millet couscous in sweetened yogurt.

desserts.name: Banan Flambe (Flambéed Banana)
instructions: Slice bananas lengthwise
Melt butter, add brown sugar — let caramelize
Add bananas, cook until soft and golden — 2-3 min per side
Add rum (carefully — off heat), return to flame to flambé
Or use orange juice for a non-alcoholic version
Add cinnamon
The sauce should be thick and caramely
Serve with vanilla ice cream if available
The French influence in Guinea — flambéed bananas with local fruit
desserts.description: Flambéed bananas — Guinea's French-influenced dessert using local fruit. Bananas caramelized in brown sugar and butter, flamed with rum. The French colonial culinary legacy meeting West African ingredients.

desserts.name: Gâteau de Patate (Sweet Potato Cake)
instructions: Boil sweet potatoes until soft, mash thoroughly
Mix with sugar, eggs, melted butter
Add flour, spices, vanilla, coconut
Pour into greased baking pan
Bake at 175°C for 40-45 min until golden and firm
The cake is dense and moist from the sweet potato
The natural sweetness of the potato means less added sugar
Let cool slightly — serve warm or at room temperature
The sweet potato turns the cake a beautiful orange-gold
desserts.description: Guinean sweet potato cake — mashed sweet potato baked into a dense, moist, golden cake spiced with cinnamon and nutmeg. The natural sweetness and color of the potato create a cake that needs less sugar and looks stunning.

drinks.name: Bissap (Hibiscus Drink)
instructions: Boil hibiscus 10 min
Strain, add sugar, mint, vanilla
Chill

drinks.name: Palm Wine
instructions: Tap palm tree for sap
Serve fresh the same day

drinks.name: Bissap (Hibiscus Tea)
instructions: Boil hibiscus flowers in water — 10-15 min
The water turns a deep, vibrant ruby red
Strain, add sugar — it needs a fair amount to balance the tartness
Add mint, vanilla, or pineapple juice for variation
Chill — serve ice cold
Bissap is drunk across all of West Africa — Guinea's version is often more concentrated
The color is stunning — deep red, almost jewel-like
Rich in vitamin C and antioxidants — it's a health drink too
Bissap is the drink of Ramadan, celebrations, and everyday life
drinks.description: Guinea's bissap — dried hibiscus flowers steeped into a deep ruby-red tea, sweetened and served ice cold. The stunning color, the tart-sweet flavor, and the health benefits make bissap one of West Africa's most photogenic and viral drinks. The Ramadan tradition adds cultural depth.

drinks.name: Jus de Gingembre (Ginger Juice)
instructions: Blend fresh ginger with water — use a LOT of ginger
Strain through fine cloth — squeeze out every drop
Add sugar, lemon juice, vanilla
The heat from the ginger should hit the back of your throat
Dilute with more water if too intense — but Guineans like it STRONG
Chill — serve ice cold
The ginger warmth in a cold drink is electrifying
Some add pineapple juice for a tropical variation
Ginger juice is considered medicinal — good for digestion, immunity, everything
drinks.description: Guinean ginger juice — fresh ginger blended and strained into an intensely fiery, sweet drink served ice cold. The throat-burning ginger heat in a cold glass is Guinean refreshment. The medicinal reputation and the fire-meets-ice concept make jus de gingembre viral.
